We did not claim any of the awards, but Treacher and Brown both carried our colours prominently. Frank Elson pleased by confirming his recent return to form, and next season he should once again be a power in our teams, as befits a Captain.
Brown, Treacher and Churcher led for three miles, but then had the misfortune to go off the course, which left Harley and Rayner in the lead.

One hundred and sixty-three competitors actually started to the signal of our President over our usual seven miles course, and from the start Johnson (Enfield), Cooper (Woodford Green), Redman (Metropolitan), Plumb (Enfield), Stone (Polytechnic) and Treacher, of ours, were prominent.
Treacher, competing for us as a team man for the first time, suffered disqualification, and Don Brown was forced to retire owing to a chilled stomach.

Brown and Treacher were together all the way until within a quarter of a mile from the finish, when Don managed to get away. Brown's walking was very jerky on occasions, and he appeared to be suffering from shin soreness.
Next year one hopes that some of our shorter distance men like Don Brown, Treacher, the brothers Churcher, and others, will venture out in this race.
Len Coleman and Bill Treacher were battling for third place until Treacher was disqualified at 1½ miles. Harry was a little too fast for Joe, and won in 14 min. 36 sec.

The chances of the A team were weakened by the disqualifications of Sutton and Treacher. This caused them to have to go into the forties for their fourth man—Stan Goold, who, by the way, is performing well this season.
